components.name: App Bar

narrative.overview: A warm paper desk with white sheets on it. Everything you enter, edit or operate, and the hard data, lies on a sheet; a page's intro and a side note lie flat on the desk, which otherwise stays empty and calm. Kan-do is a working tool that is glanced at many times a day, so the columns, the cards and the one running task have to stand clearly apart, and nothing asks for attention it has not earned.
keyCharacteristics: A warm neutral canvas, never a saturated one. Colour comes in small doses.
White sheets lifted by one warm shadow, one level only: never a sheet on a sheet.
One muted green for action and for done; orange for attention, red for what is destructive or failed.
A serif for headings, the sans for everything read and operated.
Questions are asked in place; reversible actions act at once and offer undo.
Motion is small and physical and explains a state change.
Light only (`colorMode: false`); a dark mode would be a new feature.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: One solid green button per view. A selected option (a chip, a switch, a checkbox, the funnel while a topic focus is on) may be a green fill and does not count; marks, links and the focus ring are green without being a fill. The action of a toast is soft, so a toast never adds a second lamp (user, 2026-11-20, #606).

rules.name: The Status Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Green means action or done, orange attention, red destructive or failed. None of them appears for emphasis, branding or variety (the completion burst is the one recorded exception, see "Earned celebration"); integration brand colours do not appear at all. The confirming button of a destructive dialog ("Trennen") is soft red, also when nothing is lost, like every other destructive confirm (user, 2026-11-20, #606).

rules.name: The Topic Mark Rule
rules.body: A topic carries its hue and symbol on its mark only: a small dot or glyph before the name. Never a coloured chip, card, column or surface, never a hue on a name, and no topic hue in a chart (charts use the ink ramp).

rules.name: The Marker Rule
rules.body: A stroke of yellow text marker centred on the bottom edge of a word (through the foot of its letters) is an allowed decoration in slight, intentional use (owner, 2026-11-11). It is static, carries no meaning of its own and appears once per view at most: one marker per view, on the headline of its focus column. Uses: the "Jetzt" headline on "Heute" and the "Für heute" headline (Offen) on "Alle", which fades when the user moves to "Heute" (user, #469). A second use of the hue, not of the stroke (user, #853, 2026-11-25): the paper of intro notes (the welcome, its tour, the step hints, the planning note) is the marker yellow thinned into the sheet's white, so a note reads as a note on the desk and never as a task card or a page sheet; values in `IntroNote`'s doc block. A new use is a recorded decision.

rules.name: The Frozen Primary Rule
rules.body: The primary palette (forest green, hue 152, chosen by the owner on 2026-11-11) changes only by a decision recorded here, never as a side effect of a feature.

rules.name: The Receding Text Rule
rules.body: Waiting cards, done titles and placeholders step down through a token colour, never through `opacity` on text, and keep body contrast. The recorded exceptions live with their component and in the a11y test.

rules.name: The Bright Ground Rule
rules.body: Text that is read (a brand, a headline, a summary) may lie directly on a photo only where the picture behind it is bright and even enough for WCAG AA (4.5:1, 3:1 for large text). The photo is positioned per breakpoint to guarantee that (the welcome photo is anchored to its bright wall on a phone, so the strip above the sheet shows no table, plant or book), and the contrast is checked on the rendered page at 1280 and 390 px, not assumed from the file. Flat text on the plain canvas follows "Flat intro, lifted work" (Layout); on a photo this rule decides, and a photo that cannot guarantee a bright ground behind the text gets a sheet (rule candidate #472, owner, 2026-11-18).

rules.name: The One Role Rule
rules.body: The display face is for headings only. Numerals, labels, tab names, prompts and sentences stay in the sans, at 400 to 500 (600 for a key figure).

rules.name: The One Height Rule
rules.body: Every button has the height of the main one: 36 px, 48 px on a phone, so buttons side by side line up and are as easy to hit as the main one (owner, 2026-11-17, #424). The main button differs by colour only, and a solid green or error button is at least 96 px wide. A button is smaller only where the space is narrow, and each such button is listed with its reason in `tests/config/button-ladder.test.ts`: the alert and toast action (24 px, #377), a link inside running text, and the round icon-only buttons of the board's chrome (32 px on desktop, 44 px on a phone: the Offen header's add button, the plan arrows, centred on a card's edge in the soft primary look drawn by their own rule (#467, D2), the stack header's close button) and the card-corner menu button (a 28 px circle with a 44 px hit area), whose geometry is tied to the 32 px title line and the card corner.

rules.name: The Sheets Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: A shadow belongs to a sheet: a surface lifted off the canvas that holds content. A control never casts one; a selected tab or place is a fill. The one named exception is the app bar's nav pill (flat white, no glass).

rules.name: The One Stage Rule
rules.body: The day close and the recap are one stage: the title and subline lie on the photo, anchored under the app bar, and under them sits one paper sheet in a 44 rem column that holds the content (the decks, or the summary, timebox and topics) and the two buttons, like `/welcome`: the content scrolls inside the sheet, the buttons stay at its foot under a hairline (the way out soft, the main button solid without an arrow, on top on a phone). On a window under about 30 rem tall (a landscape phone) the sheet stops scrolling inside: the whole column scrolls, the title, the content and the buttons one after the other, so nothing is cut off. On a phone the sheet floats above the tab bar with all corners rounded. The day close enters with the photo coming down over the board and both leave with it lifting. This reverses #428 (the recap's content on the photo, only the controls on a sheet) and the docked footer sheet of #612, by user decision of 2026-11-21 (#707); before that: user, 2026-11-20, #612, #580.

rules.name: The One Piece Rule
rules.body: A view arrives as one piece: incoming content does not rearrange after it is visible, a surface changes size only as a guided motion, and hover never moves a neighbour (user, ten corrections, among them #43, #225, #294).

rules.name: The Key Moment Rule
rules.body: Deliberate exception (user, 2026-11-19): a once-a-day key moment (welcome to board, recap, planning to "Heute", day close) is a full-size stage and moves slower than a mechanical change, because it is "a one-time-per-day key transition helping to tell the story" (#433); the key moments share the curtain and take `--duration-curtain` and `--duration-stage`. Challenge was: conflicts: Material's longest duration is 1000 ms, and motion here is otherwise short.

dos: **Do** follow the styling priority: (1) Nuxt UI semantic tokens (`text-muted`, `bg-elevated`, `text-primary`) → (2) baseline overrides in `assets/css/main.css` → (3) custom domain tokens in `assets/css/main.css`.
**Do** put component overrides in `app.config.ts → ui.<component>` and verify slot names via the Nuxt UI MCP `get-component-metadata` or `.nuxt/ui/<component>.ts`.

**Do** use `bg-page` for the canvas and a white sheet (`PageSheet`, the card, the task sheet, a dialog, a menu) for everything entered, edited or operated and for the hard data; a page's intro and a side note lie flat on the canvas.
**Do** name each sheet with a heading in the display face (`SectionHeader`, `PageHeader`).
**Do** take a line height from the size token of the role (`text-body` for reading text) and a duration from the duration tokens.
**Do** ask small questions in place, on the card or the row they belong to, and offer undo for reversible actions.
donts: **Don't** use raw Tailwind palette classes (`text-gray-600`, `bg-red-500`) or arbitrary hex/px values; ESLint warns on them.
**Don't** put more than one solid green button in a view, or use status colours for emphasis.
**Don't** put a shadow on a control, a sheet on a sheet, or a card in a card.
**Don't** add confirmation dialogs for reversible actions, or a dialog for a question that belongs to one card.
**Don't** stack modals or add toolbars to the board.
**Don't** animate for decoration, loop, or run board transitions during a drag.
**Don't** set numerals, labels or sentences in the display face, write a `leading-*` class, or use an icon size outside 12, 16, 20 and 24 px.
